stops.note: 'serpent', probably 'the one with the deadly glance', from derkesthai 'to see'; the Athenian lawgiver Draco (621 BC) gave us 'draconian'
Roman cavalry adopted the draco, a hollow serpent-headed windsock standard, from Sarmatian and Dacian horsemen in the 100s AD
the dragon-slaying St George became hugely popular in the West after the Crusades
the red dragon of Wales, Y Ddraig Goch, was officially recognised as the Welsh flag in 1959

current_meaning: a mythical monster like a huge reptile, often breathing fire
